item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q001_histone_related_proteins","answer":"In SCOPe, the canonical histone domain belongs to the all-alpha class (a), the Histone-fold fold (a.22), and the nucleosome-core-histone superfamily (a.22.1); the nucleosome core histone family is a.22.1.1. This family contains the four eukaryotic core histone lineages H2A, H2B, H3, and H4, their variants (for example H2A.Z and the centromeric H3 variant CENP-A), and archaeal histones such as HMf-like proteins. Their common histone-fold architecture and sequence/structural evidence support homology, although archaeal histones usually form simpler oligomers rather than eukaryotic octameric nucleosomes. Other histone-fold proteins include paired subunits of transcription complexes, notably NF-YB/NF-YC (also called CBF-B/CBF-C or HAP3/HAP5), several TFIID TAF pairs such as TAF6/TAF9 and TAF11/TAF13, and the NC2 subunits Dr1/DRAP1. SCOPe separates such histone-like transcription factors from canonical nucleosomal histones below the common a.22 fold—commonly in the histone-like-transcription-factor grouping—so sharing the fold alone is weaker evidence than membership in a.22.1 and does not justify transferring nucleosome assembly, chromatin packaging, DNA-sequence recognition, or transcriptional function. Conversely, proteins often called 'histone-like' for functional reasons—bacterial HU/IHF, H-NS and Dps, archaeal Alba, linker histone H1, and protamines—are not thereby members of the SCOPe histone fold; their resemblance is principally analogous chromatin compaction or DNA binding. For modeling, a same-family core histone is the strongest template, a same-superfamily member can support a domain-level fold model with caution about loops and oligomerization, and an a.22 fold-only match is merely a topology-level template. SCOPe classifies experimentally represented structural domains, not complete proteins or every paralog, and a representative structure must not be treated as proof that all family members have identical partners or functions.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
